text: The user attended a Billie Eilish concert at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia with their sister on 18 March 2023 and was still on a high from the experience.
The user said they are planning to buy new Billie Eilish concert merchandise online and asked for popular websites to find cool Billie Eilish gear.

The assistant recommended these websites for Billie Eilish merchandise: Billie Eilish's Official Store, Merchbar, Hot Topic, Amazon, Redbubble, Teespring and Etsy, and advised checking the authenticity and quality of items from third-party sellers.

The user asked for tips on finding rare or limited edition Billie Eilish merchandise online. The assistant suggested following her social media, signing up for her email newsletter, checking eBay and fan forums such as Reddit's r/BillieEilish, and monitoring retailers such as Urban Outfitters and Hot Topic.

The assistant said Billie Eilish has collaborated with Takashi Murakami and Fragment Design on limited edition merchandise, and suggested setting up Google Alerts or using SlingShot or Merch Informer to track rare merchandise releases.

The assistant advised acting fast when limited edition merchandise drops, since it can sell out quickly, verifying authenticity with official tags and packaging, and being patient and persistent when hunting for rare items.
The user planned to frame the concert ticket stub from the 18 March 2023 show and asked for tips on preserving it and making it look nice in a frame.

The assistant advised handling the ticket stub gently, keeping it dry and away from direct sunlight, using acid-free materials and UV-filtering glass or acrylic, and adding a caption with the concert date, venue and artist. Shadow box and floating frames were suggested.
The user planned to frame the ticket stub together with a photo of themselves and their sister from the concert and asked how to choose a good photo to pair with it.

The assistant advised choosing a photo that captures the excitement of the concert, with good lighting, clear faces looking at the camera and the concert atmosphere, and suggested printing it on high-quality paper or in black and white.
The user decided to use a selfie of themselves and their sister taken in front of the Wells Fargo Center before the concert, and asked where to print the photo in high quality.

The assistant suggested online printing services Shutterfly, Snapfish, Walgreens Photo, Costco Photo Center and Mpix, and local options CVS Photo, Walgreens, Costco, local camera stores and office supply stores.

The user said they will try Shutterfly or Snapfish to print the photo because they seem to have good reviews and a wide range of printing options, and asked how to care for the framed photo and ticket stub.
The assistant said Shutterfly and Snapfish are both well-known in the industry for their high-quality printing services.

The assistant advised caring for framed items with acid-free materials, UV-filtering glass or acrylic and secure mounting, keeping them out of direct sunlight and high humidity, storing them flat, keeping the room between 60 and 70 degrees Fahrenheit (15 to 21 Celsius), and avoiding cleaning products.

As of 1 April 2023, the user had been listening to a lot of indie music and had recently returned from a music festival in Brooklyn with a group of friends, whose lineup featured the user's favorite indie bands.

The user asked for new indie artists or bands to listen to. The assistant suggested Phoebe Bridgers, Vagabon, Soccer Mommy, The Japanese House, Glass Animals, MUNA, Sharon Van Etten, Lucy Dacus, Weyes Blood and Yumi Zouma.
The user said they saw Glass Animals live at the music festival in Brooklyn, found them amazing, and planned to check out more of their music.

The user asked for psychedelic indie-rock bands similar to Glass Animals. The assistant suggested Tame Impala, Unknown Mortal Orchestra, Pond, King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, Foxygen, Mild High Club, Temples, The Black Angels, Night Beats and The Murlocs.

The assistant said King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard are known for energetic, unpredictable live shows with extended jams, instrument swaps and crowd surfing, and that Unknown Mortal Orchestra's shows emphasize improvisation and audience interaction.

The assistant also named Pond for elaborate light shows and psychedelic visuals, Foxygen for theatrical shows led by Sam France and Jonathan Rado, and The Black Angels for dark, trippy live shows, as bands with strong live presence.

The user said they are thinking of checking out local music events, such as a free outdoor concert series in the park or a jazz night at a local bar, and asked for tips on discovering new artists in a low-key setting.

The assistant suggested discovering local acts by checking event listings, exploring local music scenes, starting with free events, arriving early, talking to locals and following local music bloggers, using platforms such as Facebook Events, Eventbrite, Meetup, Bandsintown and Songkick.

The assistant said it cannot access the user's location or personal preferences, so it could not recommend specific local events or venues, and suggested checking Eventbrite, Meetup and Facebook Events filtered by location, genre and date.

The assistant gave general tips for local music events: check the date, time, location and lineup, arrive early, dress for the weather, bring sunscreen for outdoor events, support artists by buying merchandise, and follow the artists afterwards.
The user has been listening to a lot of Queen lately and recently saw Queen perform live with Adam Lambert at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey, together with their parents.
The user said they were craving more of a classic rock sound and asked for rock music playlist recommendations on streaming services.

The assistant recommended Spotify playlists Classic Rock Essentials, Rock Anthems and The Roots of Rock, Apple Music playlists Classic Rock Radio, Rock Legends and The A-List: Classic Rock, Amazon Music playlists Classic Rock Favorites, Rock's Greatest Hits and The Classic Rock Mixtape, and Tidal playlists Classic Rock, Rock's Golden Age and The Masters of Rock.
The user said they are also interested in discovering new indie rock or alternative bands, having recently attended a music festival in Brooklyn that featured some of their favorite indie bands.

The assistant recommended indie rock bands Greta Van Fleet, Rival Sons, The Black Keys, Arctic Monkeys and Foals, alternative bands The Neighbourhood, Thirty Seconds to Mars, Panic! At The Disco, The 1975 and Bleachers, and newer bands Yungblud, The Regrettes and Palaye Royale.

The user asked about popular indie rock festivals or concerts happening in the coming months. The assistant listed the festivals Coachella, Shaky Knees, Boston Calling, Governors Ball and Lollapalooza, and tours by The 1975, Tame Impala, Arctic Monkeys, The Black Keys and Panic! At The Disco.

The assistant gave these festival dates: Coachella in Indio, CA on April 10-12 and 17-19; Shaky Knees in Atlanta, GA on May 1-3; Boston Calling in Boston, MA on May 22-24; Governors Ball in New York City on June 5-7; and Lollapalooza in Chicago, IL on July 30 to August 2.
The user said they had recently been to a music festival in Brooklyn and asked again about popular indie rock festivals or concerts happening in the coming months.

The assistant recommended festivals Panorama Music Festival in New York City on July 24-26, Forecastle in Louisville, KY on July 17-19, Outside Lands in San Francisco on August 7-9, Riot Fest in Chicago on September 11-13, and Austin City Limits in Austin, TX on October 2-4 and 9-11.
The assistant also listed touring artists Vampire Weekend, The Strokes, Orville Peck and Weyes Blood, among others, and asked which of the festivals or concerts caught the user's attention.

The user said they were really interested in the Panorama Music Festival in NYC, had heard great things about it, and asked about the festival's atmosphere, what to expect and tips for making the most of it.

The assistant described Panorama Music Festival as a three-day event on Randall's Island Park in NYC, with indie rock, alternative, electronic and hip-hop acts, a laid-back summer atmosphere, several genre stages and art installations.

The assistant advised Panorama attendees to plan a personalised itinerary, arrive early, stay hydrated with a refillable water bottle, bring sunscreen and comfortable shoes, download the official app, and buy tickets in advance because prices may rise.

The assistant said Panorama can be reached by ferry, bus or car, that three-day general admission, VIP and single-day tickets are available, and that outside food and drink are not allowed, though food and drink can be bought on site.

The user has been to a few concerts recently and attended a free outdoor concert series in the park on 25 March 2023, where they discovered some great new talent and enjoyed live music in a low-key setting.
The user said they are always looking for new artists to listen to and asked for suggestions of indie or alternative bands they might like.

The assistant suggested indie folk acts The Lumineers, Fleet Foxes, Bon Iver, The Head and the Heart and First Aid Kit, indie rock acts Arctic Monkeys, The Black Keys, Vampire Weekend, The 1975 and Tame Impala, and newer artists Mt. Joy, The Regrettes, Yungblud, Lucy Dacus and Orville Peck.
The user said they were interested in the newer artists the assistant mentioned and asked for more about Mt. Joy, including upcoming tour dates and releases.

The assistant described Mt. Joy as an American indie folk-rock band from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, formed in 2015, with members Matt Quinn (vocals, guitar), Sam Cooper (guitar), Michael Byrnes (bass), Sotiris Eliopoulos (drums) and Jackie Miclau (keyboards).

The assistant said Mt. Joy's sound blends folk, rock and pop with catchy melodies, is often compared to The Lumineers, The Head and the Heart and Mumford & Sons, and focuses on Matt Quinn's soulful vocals and storytelling lyrics.

The assistant said Mt. Joy released their self-titled debut album in 2018, featuring the hit single Alibi, and the sophomore album Rearview in 2020, with fan favorites Strangers and My Vibe. It had no official word on a new album or EP, and suggested checking the band's website or social media for tour dates.
The user said they liked the outdoor park concert series and asked for similar up-and-coming or local bands that might play at such events, similar to Mt. Joy.
The assistant suggested acts similar to Mt. Joy: The Wilder Blue (Texas), The National Parks (Utah), Caamp (West Virginia), The Lone Bellow (Brooklyn) and The Brook & The Bluff (Nashville).

The assistant suggested local and up-and-coming acts: The Western Den (Boston), The Harmaleighs (Nashville), The Talbott Brothers (Portland), The River Whyless (North Carolina) and The Foxies (Nashville).
The user said they were thinking of attending a jazz night at a local bar soon and asked which good jazz musicians or bands to look out for.

The assistant recommended modern jazz musicians Robert Glasper, Kamasi Washington, Cécile McLorin Salvant, Brad Mehldau and Esperanza Spalding, and up-and-coming jazz acts Jazzmeia Horn, Immanuel Wilkins, Joel Ross, Veronica Swift and Aaron Parks.

The assistant suggested finding local jazz talent through local jazz clubs, jazz festivals, social media, Bandcamp, SoundCloud, YouTube, music school programmes, and by asking bar staff or the musicians on the night.
The user said they might attend a music festival in the future and asked for good ones to look out for.

The assistant recommended multi-genre festivals Coachella, Lollapalooza, Bonnaroo and Outside Lands, indie and alternative festivals Sasquatch!, Governors Ball, Austin City Limits and Riot Fest, and jazz and blues festivals New Orleans Jazz & Heritage, Montreux Jazz, Monterey Jazz and Chicago Jazz Festival.
The assistant advised planning ahead because tickets and accommodation for popular festivals can sell out quickly, and suggested considering location, lineup and atmosphere when choosing a festival.

The user asked about popular jazz festivals or outdoor jazz events around this time of year. The assistant listed Montreal International Jazz Festival (late June to early July), Newport Jazz Festival (early August), Detroit Jazz Festival (Labor Day weekend), Charlie Parker Jazz Festival (late August) and San Francisco Jazz Festival (June to July).

The assistant said it does not have real-time information, so the festival timings it gave are approximate, and recommended checking dates, lineups and ticket details online, including summer jazz-in-the-park series in various cities.
The user said they had been thinking about learning the saxophone and asked whether it is a good instrument for a beginner and which online resources they would recommend.

The assistant said the saxophone can be challenging for beginners because of breath control, embouchure and finger dexterity, but is versatile across genres, suited to improvisation, and has a relatively limited range that makes notes easier to learn.

The assistant recommended online saxophone resources: YouTube channels Sax Lessons 365, Saxophone Lessons To Go and The Saxophonist; courses from Saxophone Lessons Online, ArtistWorks and TrueFire; apps Freshumi, Saxophone Fingering Chart and Transcribe!; and the community Saxontheweb.
The user said they plan to start with online lessons and YouTube tutorials and asked whether to invest in a good quality saxophone as a beginner and which brands or models to consider.

The assistant recommended student-level saxophones from Yamaha, Jupiter and Conn-Selmer, naming the Yamaha YAS-26, Jupiter JAS1100 and Conn-Selmer AS711 alto saxophones, and suggested renting before buying to test the instrument.
The assistant said beginners should budget for extras including a good mouthpiece, reeds that wear out regularly, a good quality case, and occasional maintenance and repairs.

The user asked whether finding a good teacher or instructor is important for learning the saxophone. The assistant said a teacher gives personalized guidance, corrects bad habits early, provides accountability and instant feedback, and can be found through referrals, Lessons.com, TakeLessons, Thumbtack, music stores, NATS or MTNA.
